items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "rickets"?
options: A diet containing all the nutrients in the correct proportions, and enough energy, for an individual.
A condition caused by lack of iron, in which too little haemoglobin is made.
A deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin D or calcium, in which bones are soft and bend.
Indigestible material (mainly cellulose) that adds bulk and helps peristalsis.
items.answer: A deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin D or calcium, in which bones are soft and bend.
items.markingKey: Rickets: a deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin D or calcium, in which bones are soft and bend.

items.stem: Explain why a teenager needs more protein per kilogram of body mass than an adult.
items.answer: Teenagers are growing, and protein is needed to make new cells and tissues (and enzymes).
items.markingKey: growth [1]; protein for new cells / tissues [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why people who spend little time in sunlight may develop weak bones.
items.answer: Skin makes vitamin D in sunlight; vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium; without it bones become soft (rickets).
items.markingKey: vitamin D made in sunlight [1]; needed for calcium absorption [1]; weak bones [1] [3]

items.stem: A person shows these symptoms: tiredness, lack of energy (too little haemoglobin). Which nutrient is most likely lacking from their diet?
items.answer: iron
items.markingKey: Anaemia: lack of iron.

items.stem: A child in Seoul has bleeding gums, poor wound healing. (a) Suggest the deficiency disease and the nutrient that is lacking. (b) Suggest two foods that would help prevent it.
items.answer: (a) scurvy; vitamin C (b) e.g. citrus fruit
items.markingKey: (a) scurvy [1]; vitamin C [1] (b) two suitable foods, e.g. citrus fruit [2] [4]

items.stem: Mateo burned samples of different nuts, each of mass 1.0 g, under a boiling tube containing 20 cm³ of water and recorded the temperature rise. Results table. Type of nut: peanut, cashew, walnut, almond. Temperature rise / °C, trial 1: 24, 21.8, 26.8, 21.9; trial 2: 23.8, 21.6, 27.9, 21.9; trial 3: 24.4, 22, 16.4, 23.3. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) Calculate the energy released by the peanut, using energy = 20 × 4.2 × temperature rise.
items.answer: (a) Independent: type of nut; dependent: temperature rise. (b) 2022 J
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = type of nut [1]; dependent variable = temperature rise [1] [2] (b) 20 × 4.2 × 24.07 [1] = 2022 J [1] [2]

items.stem: A sailor has bleeding gums after months without fresh fruit. Which nutrient is lacking?
items.answer: Vitamin C
items.markingKey: Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin C.

items.stem: Explain why a person with anaemia feels tired.
items.answer: Lack of iron means less haemoglobin, so the blood carries less oxygen; less aerobic respiration releases less energy.
items.markingKey: less haemoglobin [1]; less oxygen / respiration / energy [1] [2]

items.stem: Kenji burned a 0.89 g crisp under a boiling tube containing 10 cm³ of water. The temperature rose from 21.0 °C to 55.9 °C. Calculate the energy in the food per gram, in J/g. (4.2 J raise the temperature of 1 g of water by 1 °C.)

Leila burned a 0.89 g peanut under a boiling tube containing 10 cm³ of water. The temperature rose from 21.0 °C to 35.8 °C. Calculate the energy in the food per gram, in J/g. (4.2 J raise the temperature of 1 g of water by 1 °C.) The value on the food label is much higher. Suggest two reasons for the difference.
items.answer: 698 J/g; heat lost to the air / tube and the food not burned completely.
items.markingKey: ΔT = 14.8 °C [1]; energy = 10 × 4.2 × 14.8 = 621.6 J [1]; ÷ 0.89 = 698 J/g [1]; heat lost to surroundings / heating the tube [1]; incomplete combustion [1] [5]

items.stem: Nadia burned samples of different nuts, each of mass 1.0 g, under a boiling tube containing 20 cm³ of water and recorded the temperature rise. Results table. Type of nut: hazelnut, cashew, peanut, walnut. Temperature rise / °C, trial 1: 27.2, 22.8, 26.1, 29.5; trial 2: 27.6, 23.7, 25.4, 30.5; trial 3: 16.1, 23.2, 25.4, 28.4. (a) Explain the results. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) A larger temperature rise means more energy was transferred to the water, so that nut contains more energy per gram (more fat). (b) Insulate the boiling tube / use a calorimeter to reduce heat loss.
items.markingKey: (a) more temperature rise = more energy [1]; linked to fat content [1] [2] (b) Any one from: insulate the boiling tube / use a calorimeter to reduce heat loss; relight the nut until it burns completely; stir the water before reading the thermometer; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the type of nut (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: What is the name for "the movement of nutrients from the intestines into the blood"?
items.answer: Absorption
items.markingKey: Absorption: the movement of nutrients from the intestines into the blood.

items.stem: Explain how tooth decay develops.
items.answer: Bacteria in plaque feed on sugars and produce acid, which dissolves the enamel and then dentine, forming a cavity.
items.markingKey: bacteria + sugar [1]; acid [1]; enamel dissolved [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain how regular brushing and limiting sugary foods reduce tooth decay.
items.answer: Brushing removes plaque bacteria; less sugar means bacteria make less acid that dissolves enamel; fluoride toothpaste strengthens enamel.
items.markingKey: removes plaque / bacteria [1]; less acid [1] [2]

items.stem: Which organ has this function: stores bile?
items.answer: gall bladder
items.markingKey: Gall bladder: stores bile.

items.stem: State the function of each organ in digestion: (i) stomach, (ii) colon, (iii) rectum.
items.answer: (i) mechanical digestion by muscular churning; protease (pepsin) digests protein; hydrochloric acid kills pathogens (ii) absorbs water from undigested food (iii) stores faeces
items.markingKey: (i) mechanical digestion by muscular churning; protease (pepsin) digests protein; hydrochloric acid kills pathogens [1]; (ii) absorbs water from undigested food [1]; (iii) stores faeces [1] [3]

items.stem: Ethan eats a boiled egg with toast. The food passes through the alimentary canal over the next 24 hours. (a) Explain the function of the colon. (b) Describe the role of the liver and pancreas in digestion, even though food does not pass through them.
items.answer: (a) It absorbs water from the remaining undigested food, forming faeces. (b) The liver makes bile, stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum; the pancreas secretes amylase, protease and lipase into the duodenum.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] (b) liver bile [1]; pancreas enzymes [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how peristalsis moves food along the oesophagus.
items.answer: Circular and longitudinal muscles contract and relax in waves; contraction of circular muscle behind the food squeezes it forward.
items.markingKey: muscles contract in waves [1]; circular behind bolus pushes it [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the stomach wall is very muscular.
items.answer: Muscular contractions churn the food, mixing it with gastric juice and breaking it into smaller pieces (mechanical digestion).
items.markingKey: churning / mixing [1]; mechanical digestion [1] [2]

items.stem: Which type of tooth is pointed, for gripping and tearing?
items.answer: canines
items.markingKey: Canines: pointed, for gripping and tearing.

items.stem: Mohammed eats a plate of pasta with chicken. The food passes through the alimentary canal over the next 24 hours. (a) Name the organ where most nutrients are absorbed. (b) Explain the function of the colon. (c) Describe the role of the liver and pancreas in digestion, even though food does not pass through them.
items.answer: (a) Small intestine (ileum). (b) It absorbs water from the remaining undigested food, forming faeces. (c) The liver makes bile, stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum; the pancreas secretes amylase, protease and lipase into the duodenum.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) [2] (c) liver bile [1]; pancreas enzymes [1] [2]

items.stem: What is the name for "an alkaline liquid made by the liver that neutralises stomach acid and emulsifies fats"?
items.answer: Bile
items.markingKey: Bile: an alkaline liquid made by the liver that neutralises stomach acid and emulsifies fats.

items.stem: Explain why bile is needed for efficient fat digestion.
items.answer: Bile emulsifies fats into tiny droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase; it also neutralises acid, giving a suitable pH for lipase.
items.markingKey: emulsifies / surface area [1]; neutralises acid / pH for lipase [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the contents of the duodenum need to be neutralised.
items.answer: Food arrives from the stomach at pH about 2; pancreatic enzymes work best at slightly alkaline pH, so bile and pancreatic juice raise the pH.
items.markingKey: stomach contents acidic [1]; enzymes in duodenum need alkaline / neutral pH [1] [2]

items.stem: A fat droplet of radius 3 mm is emulsified by bile into 8 smaller droplets, each of radius 1.5 mm. (surface area of a sphere = 4πr²) Calculate the total surface area before and after emulsification, and the factor by which it increases.
items.answer: before 113.1 mm²; after 226.2 mm²; increase × 2

items.stem: A fat droplet of radius 3 mm is emulsified by bile into 27 smaller droplets, each of radius 1 mm. (surface area of a sphere = 4πr²) Calculate the total surface area before and after emulsification, and the factor by which it increases.
items.answer: before 113.1 mm²; after 339.3 mm²; increase × 3

items.stem: A fat droplet of radius 1 mm is emulsified by bile into 27 smaller droplets, each of radius 0.333 mm. (surface area of a sphere = 4πr²) Calculate the total surface area before and after emulsification, and the factor by which it increases. Explain why this increases the rate of fat digestion.
items.answer: before 12.6 mm²; after 37.7 mm²; increase × 3; larger surface area for lipase to act on, so more enzyme–substrate collisions.
items.markingKey: 4π × 1² = 12.6 mm² [1]; 27 × 4π × 0.333² = 37.7 mm² [1]; × 3 [1]; more surface for lipase / more collisions [1] [4]

items.stem: Mateo placed a mixture of starch and amylase in Visking tubing, stood it in a boiling tube of water at 37 °C, and tested the water outside the tubing for reducing sugar at intervals using Benedict's solution. The colour score (0 = blue, 5 = brick-red) is shown. Results table. Time / min: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Benedict's colour score: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: (a) Temperature; volume and concentration of starch. (b) Set up a tube with boiled amylase (or water) and starch; no sugar should appear outside, showing amylase is needed to digest starch.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two from: temperature; volume and concentration of starch; volume and concentration of amylase; length of Visking tubing [2] (b) 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Tomás placed a mixture of starch and amylase in Visking tubing, stood it in a boiling tube of water at 37 °C, and tested the water outside the tubing for reducing sugar at intervals using Benedict's solution. The colour score (0 = blue, 5 = brick-red) is shown. Results table. Time / min: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Benedict's colour score: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5. (a) Describe the trend shown by the results. (b) Explain the results.
items.answer: (a) The colour score increases with time: more reducing sugar appears in the water outside the tubing. (b) Amylase digests starch into maltose; maltose molecules are small enough to diffuse through the partially permeable Visking tubing, but starch and amylase molecules are too large.
items.markingKey: (a) correct overall pattern [1]; data quoted with units / turning point given [1] [2] (b) starch digested to maltose [1]; maltose small enough to pass through [1]; starch too large [1] [3]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "emulsification"?
options: A protease secreted by the pancreas that acts in the small intestine.
An enzyme on the membranes of the small intestine epithelium that breaks maltose into glucose.
A protease made in the stomach that works best in acid.
Breaking large fat droplets into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase.
items.answer: Breaking large fat droplets into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase.
items.markingKey: Emulsification: breaking large fat droplets into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase.

items.stem: What is the function of hydrochloric acid in the stomach?
options: To kill pathogens in food and give the optimum pH for pepsin
items.answer: To kill pathogens in food and give the optimum pH for pepsin
items.markingKey: The low pH (about 2) kills bacteria and suits pepsin.

items.stem: Which enzyme digests fats into fatty acids and glycerol?
items.answer: lipase
items.markingKey: Lipase: fats → fatty acids and glycerol; made in pancreas.

items.stem: Priya placed a mixture of starch and amylase in Visking tubing, stood it in a boiling tube of water at 37 °C, and tested the water outside the tubing for reducing sugar at intervals using Benedict's solution. The colour score (0 = blue, 5 = brick-red) is shown. Results table. Time / min: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Benedict's colour score: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5. Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: Set up a tube with boiled amylase (or water) and starch; no sugar should appear outside, showing amylase is needed to digest starch.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: For the enzyme protease (trypsin), state (a) its substrate, (b) its products, (c) where it is produced and (d) where it acts.
items.answer: (a) protein (b) amino acids (c) pancreas (d) duodenum
items.markingKey: (a) protein (b) amino acids (c) pancreas (d) duodenum; 1 mark each [4]

items.stem: Sofia placed a mixture of starch and amylase in Visking tubing, stood it in a boiling tube of water at 37 °C, and tested the water outside the tubing for reducing sugar at intervals using Benedict's solution. The colour score (0 = blue, 5 = brick-red) is shown. Results table. Time / min: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Benedict's colour score: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5. (a) Explain the results. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation. (c) Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: (a) Amylase digests starch into maltose; maltose molecules are small enough to diffuse through the partially permeable Visking tubing, but starch and amylase molecules are too large. (b) Use a colorimeter to measure the colour change rather than judging by eye. (c) Set up a tube with boiled amylase (or water) and starch; no sugar should appear outside, showing amylase is needed to digest starch.
items.markingKey: (a) starch digested to maltose [1]; maltose small enough to pass through [1]; starch too large [1] [3] (b) Any one from: use a colorimeter to measure the colour change rather than judging by eye; test the water with iodine to show that starch does not pass through; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the time (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1] (c) 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "hepatic portal vein"?
options: A finger-like projection of the lining of the small intestine that increases the surface area for absorption.
The blood vessel that carries absorbed nutrients from the small intestine to the liver.
A lymph vessel in the centre of a villus that absorbs fatty acids and glycerol.
Tiny projections on the surface membrane of epithelial cells of villi, further increasing surface area.
items.answer: The blood vessel that carries absorbed nutrients from the small intestine to the liver.
items.markingKey: Hepatic portal vein: the blood vessel that carries absorbed nutrients from the small intestine to the liver.

items.stem: Explain why a good blood supply to the villi increases the rate of absorption.
items.answer: Blood carries absorbed nutrients away quickly, maintaining a steep concentration gradient for diffusion.
items.markingKey: carries nutrients away [1]; maintains gradient [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the epithelial cells of villi contain many mitochondria.
items.answer: They absorb some substances, such as glucose, by active transport, which needs energy from respiration.
items.markingKey: active transport [1]; energy from respiration [1] [2]

items.stem: The inner surface of a person's small intestine would be 0.5 m² if it were a smooth tube. Folds and villi increase this 10 times and microvilli increase it a further 15 times. Calculate the total absorptive surface area.
items.answer: 75 m²

items.stem: The inner surface of a person's small intestine would be 0.3 m² if it were a smooth tube. Folds and villi increase this 12 times and microvilli increase it a further 15 times. Calculate the total absorptive surface area.
items.answer: 54 m²

items.stem: A doctor in Colombo examines a sample of the lining of the small intestine under a microscope. It has many villi, each covered by a single layer of epithelial cells with microvilli. (a) Explain why the epithelial cells contain many mitochondria. (b) Name the organ that receives absorbed glucose and amino acids first, and state one thing it does with them.
items.answer: (a) To release energy by aerobic respiration for active transport of nutrients such as glucose. (b) The liver: stores glucose as glycogen / deaminates excess amino acids.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] (b) liver [1]; function [1] [2]

items.stem: Coeliac disease damages villi, making them flatter. Explain why people with untreated coeliac disease may lose weight.
items.answer: Flattened villi have a smaller surface area, so fewer digested nutrients are absorbed into the blood.
items.markingKey: smaller surface area [1]; less absorption [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the small intestine is very long.
items.answer: A long intestine gives a large surface area and more time for digestion and absorption to be completed.
items.markingKey: surface area [1]; time [1] [2]

items.stem: The glucose concentration in blood entering the small intestine is 6.0 mmol/dm³ and in blood leaving it in the hepatic portal vein after a meal is 13.2 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate the percentage increase. (b) Name the blood vessel carrying blood from the small intestine to the liver. (c) Explain how glucose enters the blood in the villi.
items.answer: (a) 120% (b) hepatic portal vein (c) By diffusion down a concentration gradient and by active transport into epithelial cells, then into the capillaries.
items.markingKey: (a) (13.2 − 6.0) ÷ 6.0 × 100 = 120% [2] (b) hepatic portal vein [1] (c) diffusion [1]; active transport [1] [5]

items.stem: A doctor in Bangkok examines a sample of the lining of the small intestine under a microscope. It has many villi, each covered by a single layer of epithelial cells with microvilli. (a) Describe three features of villi that increase the rate of absorption. (b) Explain the role of the lacteal.
items.answer: (a) Large surface area (villi and microvilli); thin wall one cell thick; dense capillary network maintaining the concentration gradient. (b) It absorbs fatty acids and glycerol, which pass into the lymph system and later into the blood.
items.markingKey: (a) three features [3] (b) [2]

items.stem: Why does a pregnant woman need more iron in her diet?
options: To make extra haemoglobin for her own and the fetus's red blood cells
items.answer: To make extra haemoglobin for her own and the fetus's red blood cells
items.markingKey: Iron is part of haemoglobin.

items.stem: Explain why an athlete in training needs more carbohydrate than an office worker.
items.answer: More muscle activity needs more energy from respiration; carbohydrates provide glucose for respiration.
items.markingKey: more energy needed [1]; carbohydrate provides glucose for respiration [1] [2]

items.stem: A food label states 1720 kJ per 100 g. A serving is 60 g. (a) Calculate the energy in one serving. (b) Calculate the percentage of a daily requirement of 11,500 kJ that this provides.

Mei burned a 0.52 g crisp under a boiling tube containing 20 cm³ of water. The temperature rose from 21.0 °C to 54.2 °C. Calculate the energy in the food per gram, in J/g. (4.2 J raise the temperature of 1 g of water by 1 °C.)

(a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) Identify the anomalous result in the table and state what should be done with it. items.stem: Which part of the alimentary canal absorbs most water?
items.answer: Small intestine
items.markingKey: Most water is absorbed in the small intestine; the colon absorbs some more.

items.stem: Lucas says: "Food passes through the liver and pancreas as it is digested." Explain whether Lucas is correct.
items.answer: Food passes only through the alimentary canal; the liver and pancreas release bile and enzymes into the duodenum.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Food passes only through the alimentary canal; the liver and pancreas release bile and enzymes into the duodenum. [2]

items.stem: Which organ has this function: absorbs water from undigested food?
items.answer: colon
items.markingKey: Colon: absorbs water from undigested food.

items.stem: Describe the shape and function of incisors, and suggest how the teeth of a sheep are adapted to its diet.
items.answer: Incisors: chisel-shaped, for biting and cutting. A sheep: large flat molars and premolars for grinding grass; no upper incisors.
items.markingKey: incisors shape [1]; function [1]; adaptation to diet [1] [3]

items.stem: Lina eats a boiled egg with toast. The food passes through the alimentary canal over the next 24 hours. (a) Explain the function of the colon. (b) Distinguish between egestion and excretion. (c) Describe the role of the liver and pancreas in digestion, even though food does not pass through them.
items.answer: (a) It absorbs water from the remaining undigested food, forming faeces. (b) Egestion removes undigested food as faeces; excretion removes metabolic waste such as urea and CO₂. (c) The liver makes bile, stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum; the pancreas secretes amylase, protease and lipase into the duodenum.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] (b) [2] (c) liver bile [1]; pancreas enzymes [1] [2]

items.stem: What is the name for "a protease secreted by the pancreas that acts in the small intestine"?
items.answer: Trypsin
items.markingKey: Trypsin: a protease secreted by the pancreas that acts in the small intestine.

items.stem: Explain why large molecules must be digested before absorption.
items.answer: They are too large and insoluble to pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood; small soluble molecules can be absorbed.
items.markingKey: large / insoluble [1]; small molecules absorbed [1] [2]

items.stem: Describe how starch is digested completely to glucose in humans.
items.answer: Amylase from salivary glands and the pancreas breaks starch into maltose; maltase on the membranes of the small intestine epithelium breaks maltose into glucose.
items.markingKey: amylase → maltose [1]; sources [1]; maltase → glucose [1] [3]

items.stem: Where is maltase produced?
items.answer: epithelium of small intestine
items.markingKey: Maltase is produced in the epithelium of small intestine.

items.stem: Where is lipase produced?
items.answer: pancreas
items.markingKey: Lipase is produced in the pancreas.

items.stem: Ana set up three tubes each containing milk (which contains fat), lipase and sodium carbonate solution (pH 8.0), with phenolphthalein indicator (pink in alkali, colourless at pH below 8.3). Tube A: lipase + bile salts; tube B: lipase only; tube C: boiled lipase. Times for the pink colour to disappear were A: 4 min, B: 11 min, C: no change after 30 min. (a) Calculate how many times faster the reaction was in tube A than in tube B. (b) State two variables that should be kept constant.
items.answer: (a) 2.75 times (b) Temperature; volume of milk / lipase / indicator; concentration of lipase.

items.stem: Lina says: "Digested food is absorbed in the stomach." Explain whether Lina is correct.
items.answer: Most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine through the villi.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine through the villi. [2]

items.stem: Omar writes in a revision note: "Villi absorb food by osmosis." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Villi absorb nutrients by diffusion and active transport; water is absorbed by osmosis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Villi absorb nutrients by diffusion and active transport; water is absorbed by osmosis. [2]

items.stem: The glucose concentration in blood entering the small intestine is 8.0 mmol/dm³ and in blood leaving it in the hepatic portal vein after a meal is 12.4 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate the percentage increase. (b) Name the blood vessel carrying blood from the small intestine to the liver.
items.answer: (a) 55% (b) hepatic portal vein

items.stem: Describe how the structure of the small intestine is adapted for the absorption of digested food.
items.answer: Very long; folded inner wall; villi and microvilli give huge surface area; epithelium one cell thick; capillary network and lacteals; good blood supply maintains gradient; mitochondria for active transport.
items.markingKey: any five adaptations linked to absorption [5]

items.stem: Which nutrient helps prevent constipation?
items.answer: Dietary fibre
items.markingKey: Fibre adds bulk, helping peristalsis.

items.stem: Mohammed says: "A balanced diet means eating equal amounts of every food group." Explain whether Mohammed is correct.
items.answer: A balanced diet contains all nutrients in the correct proportions for that person, not equal amounts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: A balanced diet contains all nutrients in the correct proportions for that person, not equal amounts. [2]

Explain what is meant by a balanced diet and how dietary needs change with age, activity and pregnancy.
items.answer: All seven nutrient groups in the right proportions with energy matching needs. Growing children need more protein and calcium per kg; active people need more energy; pregnant women need more iron, calcium, folic acid and protein; elderly need less energy.

items.stem: Which teeth are used for crushing and grinding food?
items.answer: Molars
items.markingKey: Molars and premolars have cusps for grinding.

items.stem: A student in Jakarta states: "Mechanical digestion breaks large molecules into small molecules." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces; chemical digestion breaks large molecules into small ones.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces; chemical digestion breaks large molecules into small ones. [2]

items.stem: Which organ has this function: first part of the small intestine where pancreatic juice and bile are added?
items.answer: duodenum
items.markingKey: Duodenum: first part of the small intestine where pancreatic juice and bile are added.

items.stem: State the function of each organ in digestion: (i) duodenum, (ii) gall bladder, (iii) colon.
items.answer: (i) first part of the small intestine where pancreatic juice and bile are added (ii) stores bile (iii) absorbs water from undigested food
items.markingKey: (i) first part of the small intestine where pancreatic juice and bile are added [1]; (ii) stores bile [1]; (iii) absorbs water from undigested food [1] [3]

items.stem: Kwame eats a cheese sandwich. The food passes through the alimentary canal over the next 24 hours. (a) Describe the role of the teeth and the stomach in mechanical digestion. (b) Name the organ where most nutrients are absorbed. (c) Explain the function of the colon.
items.answer: (a) Teeth cut and grind food into smaller pieces; the muscular stomach wall churns the food; both increase the surface area for enzymes. (b) Small intestine (ileum). (c) It absorbs water from the remaining undigested food, forming faeces.
items.markingKey: (a) teeth [1]; stomach churning [1]; surface area [1] [3] (b) [1] (c) [2]

items.stem: Which term is defined as "an enzyme on the membranes of the small intestine epithelium that breaks maltose into glucose"?
items.answer: Maltase
items.markingKey: Maltase: an enzyme on the membranes of the small intestine epithelium that breaks maltose into glucose.

items.stem: A person has their gall bladder removed. Suggest why they are advised to eat a low-fat diet.
items.answer: Bile is no longer stored and released in large amounts after a meal, so fats are less emulsified and digested more slowly.
items.markingKey: less bile released [1]; poorer fat emulsification / digestion [1] [2]

items.stem: Ravi writes in a revision note: "Bile is an enzyme that digests fat." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Bile contains no enzymes; it emulsifies fat so that lipase can digest it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Bile contains no enzymes; it emulsifies fat so that lipase can digest it. [2]

items.stem: Yusuf placed a mixture of starch and amylase in Visking tubing, stood it in a boiling tube of water at 37 °C, and tested the water outside the tubing for reducing sugar at intervals using Benedict's solution. The colour score (0 = blue, 5 = brick-red) is shown. Results table. Time / min: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Benedict's colour score: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5. Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: Use a colorimeter to measure the colour change rather than judging by eye.
items.markingKey: Any one from: use a colorimeter to measure the colour change rather than judging by eye; test the water with iodine to show that starch does not pass through; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the time (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Where is protease (trypsin) produced?
items.answer: pancreas
items.markingKey: Protease (trypsin) is produced in the pancreas.

items.stem: Mei placed a mixture of starch and amylase in Visking tubing, stood it in a boiling tube of water at 37 °C, and tested the water outside the tubing for reducing sugar at intervals using Benedict's solution. The colour score (0 = blue, 5 = brick-red) is shown. Results table. Time / min: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Benedict's colour score: 0, 1, 2, 4, 5. (a) Describe the trend shown by the results. (b) Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: (a) The colour score increases with time: more reducing sugar appears in the water outside the tubing. (b) Set up a tube with boiled amylase (or water) and starch; no sugar should appear outside, showing amylase is needed to digest starch.
items.markingKey: (a) correct overall pattern [1]; data quoted with units / turning point given [1] [2] (b) 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Noah writes in a revision note: "Digested food is absorbed in the stomach." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine through the villi.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine through the villi. [2]

items.stem: A student in Nairobi states: "Villi absorb food by osmosis." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Villi absorb nutrients by diffusion and active transport; water is absorbed by osmosis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Villi absorb nutrients by diffusion and active transport; water is absorbed by osmosis. [2]

items.stem: The glucose concentration in blood entering the small intestine is 6.0 mmol/dm³ and in blood leaving it in the hepatic portal vein after a meal is 8.0 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate the percentage increase. (b) Name the blood vessel carrying blood from the small intestine to the liver.
items.answer: (a) 33.3% (b) hepatic portal vein

items.stem: A doctor in Istanbul examines a sample of the lining of the small intestine under a microscope. It has many villi, each covered by a single layer of epithelial cells with microvilli. (a) Describe three features of villi that increase the rate of absorption. (b) Explain why water absorption in the small intestine is described as osmosis.
items.answer: (a) Large surface area (villi and microvilli); thin wall one cell thick; dense capillary network maintaining the concentration gradient. (b) As nutrients are absorbed, the cells and blood have a lower water potential than the gut contents, so water moves into them through partially permeable membranes.
items.markingKey: (a) three features [3] (b) water potential gradient [1]; partially permeable membrane [1] [2]
